items.action: Patch the Nov 12 deadline batch before end of day; Barracuda ESG and Chrome fixes follow by Nov 13.
items.details: The Nov 12 deadline batch includes GPUStack CVE-2026-102895 (9.8, unauthenticated admin access), FreeSwitch CVE-2026-116779 (9.8, code injection), IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218 (9.8, privilege escalation) and OpenSSH 'SSHole'. The Nov 10 additions include Chrome CVE-2026-125350 (8.8, exploited) and Barracuda CVE-2026-116606 (9.3) and CVE-2026-111560 (8.6), with a Nov 13 deadline.
items.summary: CISA added exploited flaws in Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Outlook, Chrome and Cisco BroadWorks to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 10. Four earlier additions — GPUStack, FreeSwitch, IBM Aspera Faspex and OpenSSH — carry a federal patch deadline of today, Nov 12.
items.title: CISA KEV deadline hits today: exploited Barracuda, Outlook, Chrome and Cisco flaws added

items.action: Update PHP to the patched versions and redeploy affected applications immediately.
items.details: The flaws were disclosed by Wiz Research with Google Cloud after AI-assisted research. Cloudflare said it saw thousands of exploitation attempts in the 10 hours before public announcement and has deployed mitigations for all customers; companies and government agencies in several countries temporarily restricted some online services as a precaution while patching.
items.summary: CERT-In issued a critical-severity warning over two PHP vulnerabilities with confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild. The flaws could let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely and disclose memory on affected systems.
items.title: Critical PHP flaws under large-scale exploitation; CERT-In urges urgent patching

items.action: Upgrade Apache HTTP Server to 2.4.71 and Node.js to 26.13.1, 24.22.3 or 22.23.5.
items.details: The Apache flaw was found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and Google Cloud analysts; no exploitation has been reported yet. Node's fixes also cover HTTP/2 use-after-free flaws (CVE-2026-123866, CVE-2026-123874) and an SNI-based mTLS client-certificate bypass (CVE-2026-123872).
items.summary: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71, released Nov 11, fixes a critical race condition in mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618) that can lead to remote code execution on versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The same day, Node.js 26.13.1, 24.22.3 and 22.23.5 patched 16 CVEs, including a cross-connection heap leak that can expose TLS private keys (CVE-2026-123864).
items.title: Apache httpd 2.4.71 fixes critical mod_http2 RCE; Node.js patches 16 CVEs

items.action: Check Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-219 for fixed releases and patch; restrict management interfaces to trusted networks.
items.details: Affected versions include FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7 and 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, plus the Cloud editions. The CVE record listed no fixed version at publication; Fortinet's advisory is FG-IR-26-219. No exploitation has been reported yet.
items.summary: CVE-2026-126170, published Nov 11, is an improper output-encoding flaw in FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (including Cloud and BigData editions) that may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorised code or commands via a specially crafted HTTP request.
items.title: FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-126170, CVSS 9.8)

items.action: Logistics customers should watch for phishing using driver and shipment data; Maersk says operations and bookings continue as usual.
items.details: WhiteArmor claims the data came from the OCF/LF Logistics platform and includes nearly 30,000 driver records, plaintext passwords and 27,842 mobile device logs with phone numbers, emails and IMEI numbers. Maersk says its findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data was disclosed and no other systems were impacted, and it has not linked the incident to WhiteArmor by name. The gang's claims are unverified.
items.summary: Maersk confirmed on Nov 11 that an attacker accessed and extracted data from a local legacy system inherited through a previous acquisition. The WhiteArmor ransomware gang claims about 100GB of data and is demanding $5 million in bitcoin within 30 days.
items.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware gang demands $5 million

items.action: Treat as an unverified actor claim for now; watch for phishing built on identity-graph and hashed-email data.
items.details: The claimed haul includes 1,006 per-client audience delivery files (220.5GB) spanning purchase, OTT, demographics and predictive segments, plus device refinement and compliance opt-out feeds dated October 2026. The claim has not been independently verified.
items.summary: The N0n ransomware group claims it exfiltrated 39,055 files totalling over 2.2 terabytes from LiveRamp, a US data-collaboration and identity-resolution company, including identity graph feeds and 19.2 million hashed email identities. The data is listed as exposed and not paid.
items.title: N0n ransomware claims 2.2TB theft from LiveRamp, including 19.2M hashed email identities

items.action: DraftKings customers should watch for phishing using old contact details; no current credential exposure is claimed.
items.details: The exposed set also includes campaign demographic analytics from November 2019 covering age, gender, language, handset, carrier and app profiles across 11,421 devices. The data is historical, not current account credentials.
items.summary: The N0n ransomware group listed DraftKings on Nov 11, exposing historical consumer data: 6.3 million mobile device advertising identifiers from 2020 and 7.4 million hashed consumer email addresses from 2020, marked 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED'.
items.title: N0n lists DraftKings, exposing 6.3M device IDs and 7.4M hashed emails from 2020

items.action: Verify no reliance on eMudhra intermediate certificates remains in your trust stores; treat certificates chaining to them as untrusted.
items.details: Sixteen intermediate key pairs were correctly generated on an HSM on April 30, 2025, but a wrap-unwrap script read the private keys back incorrectly, weakening them far below the intended 384-bit strength. eMudhra revoked eight additional RSA key pairs on Nov 7, has exited the global digital-certificate business, and a KPMG independent review is due by Dec 4, 2026.
items.summary: eMudhra's full post-incident report, published Nov 10, blames a bug in its own Python key-handling script that truncated intermediate CA private keys — the smallest to the single byte '4' — leaving eight intermediate certificates (six TLS, two code-signing) weak enough for attackers to forge.
items.title: eMudhra: coding error shrank CA private keys to as little as '4'

items.action: Update Google Chrome to the latest version on all devices now.
items.details: The advisory covers Chrome versions older than 157.0.8103.50 and Chrome Extended Stable versions older than 156.0.8078.96. The flaws could let attackers take control of a device.
items.summary: CERT-In advisory CIVN-2026-0544, published Nov 10, rates multiple Google Chrome vulnerabilities critical and urges users in India to update immediately. One flaw, CVE-2026-125350, is already being actively exploited in the wild.
items.title: CERT-In flags critical Chrome flaws, urges Indian users to update now

items.action: Check for bank accounts opened in your name that you did not authorise; report unknown accounts to the bank and the national cybercrime portal.
items.details: The accused, Naveen Hussain, allegedly operated an HDFC Bank Customer Service Point centre in Jalukbari, Guwahati. Investigators found several lakh rupees deposited in accounts linked to him and suspect he may be part of a larger network involved in fraudulent banking transactions.
items.summary: Assam CID's Cyber Cell arrested a Guwahati man who allegedly posed as an HDFC Bank employee and opened multiple bank accounts in people's names without their knowledge or consent, suspected of using them to receive cyber-fraud proceeds.
items.title: Guwahati man arrested for opening fake bank accounts in HDFC employee's name
